overview.headline: Earthquake magnitude, energy and shaking intensity explained

keyPoints.point: Students learn that magnitude measures earthquake size as a single value for each event.
keyPoints.quote: Magnitude is the size of the earthquake.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that each whole number increase in magnitude means tenfold greater measured amplitude.
keyPoints.quote: each whole number increase in magnitude represents a tenfold increase in measured amplitude as measured on a seismogram

keyPoints.point: Students learn that each magnitude step releases about 32 times more energy.
keyPoints.quote: While each whole number increase in magnitude represents a tenfold increase in the measured amplitude, it represents an 32 times more energy release.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that shaking intensity varies by location and distance from fault rupture.
keyPoints.quote: The intensity is the measure of shaking at each location, and this varies from place to place

keyPoints.point: Students learn that seismic moment depends on rigidity, fault area and slip distance.
keyPoints.quote: where rigidity is the strength of the rock along the fault, area is the area of the fault that slipped, and slip is the distance the fault moved.

keyTerms.gloss: Size of an earthquake reported as one value for the whole event
keyTerms.quote: Magnitude is the size of the earthquake.

keyTerms.gloss: Measure of shaking at a place that varies with distance and ground type
keyTerms.quote: The intensity is the measure of shaking at each location, and this varies from place to place

keyTerms.gloss: Computed quantity from fault properties that is converted to moment magnitude
keyTerms.quote: First the seismic moment is computed

keyTerms.gloss: Strength of rock along a fault that helps set seismic moment size
keyTerms.quote: where rigidity is the strength of the rock along the fault

keyTerms.gloss: Measured size of ground motion recorded on a seismogram
keyTerms.quote: each whole number increase in magnitude represents a tenfold increase in measured amplitude as measured on a seismogram

keyTerms.gloss: Total shaking energy radiated by an earthquake that reflects damage potential
keyTerms.quote: it represents an 32 times more energy release.
